q: Issues of stores from a depot are ordinarily made from the oldest stock of the item held in the depot, and not from the lot most recently received. The practice is followed principally in order to:

options.A: Exhaust the old stock at its original purchase rate for the priced accounts
options.B: Enable the storekeeper to dispense with the bin cards of the item
options.C: Ensure that the freshest stock is always issued to the consuming departments
options.D: Prevent deterioration and obsolescence of stores by ensuring that stock is consumed in the order in which it was received

e: Issuing oldest stock first, on the FIFO principle, ensures stock is consumed in the order received and prevents deterioration and obsolescence of stores lying in the depot.

q: During a depot inspection, a quantity of paints is found lying in stock well beyond its prescribed shelf life and it is no longer fit for use. The correct course in respect of such stores is that they are:

options.A: Placed before the Survey Committee for condemnation and disposal, having become unserviceable
options.B: Issued to a consuming department at a reduced rate fixed by the storekeeper
options.C: Mixed with fresh stock of paints and issued in the ordinary course
options.D: Returned to the supplier for replacement free of cost in all cases

e: Stores beyond shelf life and unfit for use are unserviceable stores; they must be placed before the Survey Committee for condemnation and disposal, not issued or mixed with fresh stock.

q: A firm which is exempted from furnishing Earnest Money Deposit in a stores tender is, on acceptance of its tender, nevertheless required to:

options.A: Furnish Earnest Money Deposit at double the normal rate
options.B: Deposit the full value of the order in cash in advance
options.C: Furnish the Security Deposit prescribed under the contract, the exemption from Earnest Money Deposit not extending to Security Deposit
options.D: Execute a fresh Proprietary Article Certificate for the item

e: Exemption from Earnest Money Deposit does not extend to Security Deposit. An EMD-exempt firm must still furnish the prescribed Security Deposit on acceptance of its tender.

q: In a stores tender, the rates received are considered high and negotiations are proposed to be held with the second-lowest tenderer, the lowest tenderer being available for negotiation. This proposal is not in order because negotiations, where they become unavoidable, are held:

options.A: With all the tenderers simultaneously in an open meeting
options.B: Only with the lowest tenderer (L1), in exceptional circumstances
options.C: With the highest tenderer, whose rates have the largest margin for reduction
options.D: With the members of the Tender Committee themselves

e: Negotiations in stores tenders, where unavoidable, are held only with the lowest tenderer (L1) and only in exceptional circumstances; negotiating with L2 while L1 is available is irregular.

q: The period of validity of the offers in a stores tender has expired and the tender has not yet been decided. At this stage the tender can be accepted:

options.A: At any time thereafter, the validity period having no binding effect
options.B: Orally by the depot officer, without reference to the tenderer
options.C: Only by the Railway Board, whatever the value of the tender
options.D: Only with the consent of the tenderer, acceptance after the expiry of validity being otherwise not binding on him

e: An offer can be accepted after its validity expires only with the tenderer's consent, because after expiry the tenderer is no longer bound by the offer.

q: In a two-packet stores tender, the technical bid of a tenderer is found unacceptable by the Tender Committee. In regard to the price packet submitted by that tenderer, the correct course is that:

options.A: It is not opened, price bids being opened only of those tenderers whose techno-commercial bids are found acceptable
options.B: It is opened first, to see whether his rate is the lowest
options.C: It is opened along with all the other price packets as a matter of course
options.D: It is returned to the tenderer unopened only after the contract is placed on another firm

e: In the two-packet system, price bids are opened only for tenderers whose techno-commercial bids are found acceptable; the price packet of a technically rejected tenderer is not opened.

q: A purchase office is procuring, in one proceeding, common-use office goods which are available on a national online marketplace, and, in another, a railway-specific stores item which must be tendered among approved sources. The correct pairing of the two procurements is:

options.A: Both procurements are made by e-auction on IREPS
options.B: The office goods are tendered on IREPS and the railway-specific item is bought on GeM
options.C: The common-use goods are procured through GeM, the national marketplace for common-use goods and services, while the railway-specific stores item is procured through tendering on IREPS, the Railways' own e-procurement system
options.D: Both procurements are made by direct cash purchase by the depot storekeeper

e: Common-use goods and services are procured through GeM, the national marketplace, while railway-specific stores are procured through tendering on IREPS, the Railways' e-procurement system.

q: A stores contract is placed at the rate of Rs 260 per unit. During the currency of the contract, the supplier sells the same item to another buyer at Rs 240 per unit, and the contract contains a fall clause. The rate payable by the Railway for supplies under its contract is:

options.A: Rs 260 per unit, the contract rate remaining unaltered
options.B: Rs 250 per unit, being the average of the two rates
options.C: Rs 130 per unit, being half the rate charged to the other buyer
options.D: Rs 240 per unit, the lower rate charged to the other buyer applying to the railway contract under the fall clause

e: Under the fall clause, the lower rate of Rs 240 charged to another buyer applies to the railway contract, so the Railway pays Rs 240 per unit instead of the contract rate of Rs 260.

q: A stores contract containing a price variation clause stipulates that the price payable shall vary in proportion to a specified index named in the contract. The contract rate is Rs 800 per unit and the specified index falls from 125 to 120 during the currency of the contract. The revised rate payable per unit, worked out as stipulated in the contract, is:
e: With price variation in proportion to the index, revised rate = Rs 800 x 120/125 = Rs 800 x 0.96 = Rs 768 per unit.

q: A purchase order is placed for 2,000 units of an item at Rs 75 per unit. The Railway later exercises the option clause in the order and calls for an additional quantity of 500 units on the same terms and rate. The value of the additional quantity supplied under the option clause is:
e: Under the option clause the additional quantity is at the same rate: 500 units x Rs 75 = Rs 37,500.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 60 lakh. In its Stores Budget for the year, the anticipated debits (value of stores to be purchased and received) are Rs 2.40 crore and the anticipated credits (value of stores to be issued and sold) are Rs 2.55 crore. The closing balance of stores anticipated at the end of the year is:
e: Closing balance = opening balance + anticipated debits - anticipated credits = Rs 60 lakh + Rs 240 lakh - Rs 255 lakh = Rs 45 lakh.

q: During a year, the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is debited with Rs 2,10,000 on account of shortages and Rs 40,000 on account of downward revisions of book rates, and credited with Rs 75,000 on account of excesses found in stock verification and Rs 25,000 on account of the excess of sale value over book value of scrap sold. The net balance of the account for the year is:

options.D: Nil, the debits and credits being equal

e: Debits are Rs 2,10,000 + Rs 40,000 = Rs 2,50,000; credits are Rs 75,000 + Rs 25,000 = Rs 1,00,000. Net balance is a debit of Rs 1,50,000 in the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A stores depot issues 640 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 55 per unit to a consuming department. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issues are valued at book rate: 640 units x Rs 55 = Rs 35,200, debited to the consuming department for the stores issued.

q: During stock verification, 45 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 280 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Excess found on stock verification is taken into stock at book rate: 45 units x Rs 280 = Rs 12,600, credited through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 28 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 475 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Shortage found on verification is valued at book rate: 28 units x Rs 475 = Rs 13,300, to be accounted for through the Stock Adjustment Account after investigation.

q: A depot holds 1,600 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 64 to Rs 72 per unit. The increase in the value of the stock in hand, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:

options.A: A debit of Rs 12,800 to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: A credit of Rs 12,800 to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: A credit of Rs 1,15,200 to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: A debit of Rs 1,02,400 to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Rate rise increases stock value by 1,600 x (Rs 72 - Rs 64) = Rs 12,800. Stock is debited and the Stock Adjustment Account is credited with this increase.

q: A depot issues 300 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 140 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 15 per cent of the book value, as given in the conditions of issue. The total amount recoverable from the outside party is:
e: Book value is 300 x Rs 140 = Rs 42,000. Adding departmental charges at 15 per cent, Rs 6,300, the amount recoverable from the outside party is Rs 48,300.

q: An imported stores item is invoiced at Rs 2,60,000. The freight paid on it is Rs 24,000, the insurance premium Rs 6,000 and the customs duty Rs 30,000. The value at which the item is taken into stock in the priced accounts (its landed cost) is:
e: Landed cost = invoice + freight + insurance + customs duty = Rs 2,60,000 + Rs 24,000 + Rs 6,000 + Rs 30,000 = Rs 3,20,000, at which the item is taken into stock.

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot delays lifting the material for 8 days beyond the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 450 per day for the period of delay, as per the conditions of sale given to him. The ground rent payable by him is:
e: Ground rent for delayed lifting = 8 days x Rs 450 per day = Rs 3,600, payable by the purchaser under the conditions of sale.

q: A field official holds a stores imprest of a fixed quantity of 650 units of an item. At the time of replenishment he holds 260 units on hand and renders an account of consumption of 390 units. The quantity to be supplied to him in replenishment is:
e: In a fixed imprest, replenishment equals consumption accounted for: 650 - 260 on hand = 390 units, restoring the imprest to its fixed quantity.

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item is 10,800 units and coverage for six months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 900 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 600 units. The quantity required to be ordered is:
e: Quantity required for 6 months = AAC x 6/12 = 5,400 units. Less stock 900 and dues 600 already available, quantity to order = 5,400 - 1,500 = 3,900 units.

q: The Turnover Ratio of the stores of a railway is 0.25 and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 3.2 crore. The closing balance of stores of the railway is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues. Hence closing balance = 0.25 x Rs 3.2 crore = Rs 80 lakh.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 88 lakh and the closing balance is Rs 72 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock held = (opening balance + closing balance) / 2 = (Rs 88 lakh + Rs 72 lakh) / 2 = Rs 80 lakh.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 1.2 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 20 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual carrying cost = 20 per cent of average stock value = 0.20 x Rs 1.2 crore = Rs 24 lakh per annum.

q: Orders for an item are placed in Economic Order Quantities, and the annual ordering cost of the item works out to Rs 4,800. On the principle underlying the Economic Order Quantity, the annual inventory carrying cost of the item and the total of the two costs are:
e: At the Economic Order Quantity, annual ordering cost equals annual carrying cost. So carrying cost is also Rs 4,800 and the total of the two costs is Rs 9,600.

q: During agreement of a depot's records, the bin card of an item shows 40 units in the bin while the folio of the same item in the Priced Stores Ledger shows a balance of 38 units. The correct course in such a case is to:

options.A: Alter the bin card at once to agree with the priced ledger, without any enquiry
options.B: Investigate the difference between the custody account and the priced account, and adjust it only after the cause is established and approval obtained
options.C: Treat the two units as the storekeeper's personal property
options.D: Ignore the difference, as custody and priced accounts are never compared

e: A difference between bin card (custody account) and Priced Stores Ledger (priced account) must be investigated and adjusted only after the cause is established and approval obtained, not altered at once.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Stores Budget of a railway:
1. The anticipated debits of the budget represent the value of stores expected to be purchased and received during the year.
2. The anticipated credits of the budget represent the value of stores expected to be issued and sold during the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: In the Stores Budget, anticipated debits represent stores expected to be purchased and received, and anticipated credits represent stores expected to be issued and sold; both statements are correct.

q: A purchaser has lifted the scrap sold to him, but a part of the sale value deposited by him still remains to be finally adjusted in the books. The amount so remaining, representing sale value received but not yet finally adjusted after delivery, is held under:

options.A: Sales Suspense, as a credit balance pending final adjustment
options.B: Purchase Suspense, as a debit balance
options.C: Stock Adjustment Account, as a debit balance
options.D: Traffic Suspense, as a credit balance

e: Sale value received but not yet finally adjusted after delivery remains as a credit balance under Sales Suspense pending final adjustment in the books.

q: In FSN analysis carried out in a stores depot, an item which is drawn from stock every day in the ordinary course of working is classified as:
e: In FSN analysis, items drawn from stock frequently, such as daily in ordinary working, are classified as Fast-moving; S is slow-moving and N is non-moving.

q:
Consider the following statements about selective inventory control:
1. Under ABC analysis, control is exercised most rigorously over the items which account for the bulk of the annual consumption value.
2. An item which is vital in use is watched closely even if its annual consumption value is low.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: ABC control is strictest for items forming the bulk of annual consumption value, and VED criticality requires close watch on vital items even at low value; both statements are correct.

q: Unserviceable stores lying in a depot have been examined by the Survey Committee, which has recommended that they be condemned and surveyed off. Before the condemned stores are offered for sale, they are ordinarily:

options.A: Formed into lots and listed in an auction catalogue for sale by e-auction
options.B: Issued free of cost to the staff of the depot
options.C: Returned to the suppliers who originally supplied them
options.D: Transferred to the Dead Stock Register as tools and plant

e: Unserviceable stores surveyed off by the Survey Committee are formed into lots and listed in an auction catalogue for disposal by e-auction.

q:
Consider the following statements about procurement against a Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC):
1. The certificate records that the article is manufactured or supplied only by a particular firm.
2. Because competition is not possible for such an article, the procurement is made by single tender from that firm.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A PAC records that the article is made or supplied only by a particular firm, so competition is not possible and procurement is by single tender from that firm; both statements are correct.

q: A purchase office requires a railway-specific component which is not a common-use item and is not available on the Government e-Marketplace. The procurement is correctly made by:

options.A: Direct purchase from a local shop without any tender, whatever the value
options.B: Treating the item as scrap and selling it by e-auction
options.C: Postponing the procurement until the item appears on the marketplace
options.D: Inviting tenders through the Railways' own e-procurement system, IREPS

e: A railway-specific item not available on GeM is procured by inviting tenders through IREPS, the Railways' own e-procurement system, not by direct purchase regardless of value.

q: Through the user depot module of the integrated material management system, a consuming department is able to perform which of the following functions?

options.A: Pass the bills of suppliers for payment
options.B: Raise its demands on the stores depot online after viewing the stock position of items
options.C: Fix the Average Annual Consumption of A-category items
options.D: Conduct the e-auction of scrap lots

e: Through the user depot module of the integrated material management system (IMMS), a consuming department can view stock position and raise its demands on the stores depot online.

q: During programmed stock verification of a depot, the stock verifier finds 12 units of an item physically in excess of the book balance. The document in which this difference is recorded for further action is the:

options.A: Stock sheet, which is prepared for an excess as well as for a shortage
options.B: Receipt Note, which is issued for all excess stock found
options.C: Narrative report, which alone records all quantity differences
options.D: Issue Note, which is issued to remove the excess from the depot

e: Differences found in programmed stock verification, whether excess or shortage, are recorded in a stock sheet prepared by the stock verifier for further action and adjustment.

q: The total issues of stores of a railway are Rs 4 crore in each of two successive years. In the first year its Turnover Ratio is 0.20 and in the second year it is 0.30. The increase in the closing balance of stores between the two years is:

options.D: Nil, as the total issues are unchanged

e: Year 1 closing = 0.20 x Rs 4 crore = Rs 80 lakh; Year 2 closing = 0.30 x Rs 4 crore = Rs 120 lakh. The increase in closing balance is Rs 40 lakh.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 5,000 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 80 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 5 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 5,000 x 80 / 5) = square root of 1,60,000 = 400 units, balancing ordering and carrying costs.

q: The average consumption of an item is 130 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 4 weeks. A safety (buffer) stock of 180 units is provided for the item. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 130 x 4 + 180 = 520 + 180 = 700 units.

q: The Stores Monthly Summary, on the basis of which the stores accounts of a railway are compiled, is prepared by a depot from its records of:

options.A: Receipts and issues of stores effected during the month
options.B: Tenders invited and opened during the month
options.C: Demands which could not be met during the month
options.D: Staff present on duty during the month

e: The Stores Monthly Summary, from which monthly stores accounts are compiled, is prepared by the depot from its records of receipts and issues of stores during the month.

q: An item held in a depot has not been issued at all during the last 30 months. The consuming department states that it does not expect to require the item during the next two years, though it may require it thereafter. For the purposes of stores classification, the item is correctly treated as:

options.A: Surplus stores, but not dead surplus, in all cases
options.B: An insurance spare, to be retained indefinitely

e: An item with no issue for 30 months and not expected to be required during the next two years is treated as dead surplus stores for stores classification and disposal action.

q: A purchase order is placed for 500 units of an item at Rs 320 per unit. During the currency of the order, the Railway exercises the option clause and calls for an additional quantity of 150 units on the same terms and at the same rate. The value of the additional quantity so ordered is:
e: Under the option clause, the additional quantity is supplied at the same rate: 150 units x Rs 320 = Rs 48,000.

q: A stores contract is placed at the rate of Rs 480 per unit. During the currency of the contract, the supplier sells the same item to another buyer at Rs 450 per unit. By virtue of the fall clause in the contract, the rate payable by the Railway for supplies made thereafter is:

options.B: Rs 480 per unit, as the contract rate cannot be altered
options.C: Rs 465 per unit, being the average of the two rates
options.D: Rs 430 per unit, after a further deduction for the default

e: Under the fall clause, the lower rate of Rs 450 at which the supplier sold to another buyer becomes payable by the Railway for supplies made thereafter.

q: A stores contract containing a price variation clause stipulates that the price payable shall vary in proportion to a specified index named in the contract. The contract rate is Rs 750 per unit and the specified index rises from 100 to 108 during the currency of the contract. The revised price payable per unit is:

options.D: Rs 750 per unit, the index being irrelevant to the price

e: With price variation in proportion to the index, revised price = Rs 750 x 108/100 = Rs 810 per unit.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 2,40,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 3 weeks late. Liquidated damages are leviable at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay, as stipulated in the contract. The liquidated damages recoverable are:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5 per cent of Rs 2,40,000 per week x 3 weeks = Rs 1,200 x 3 = Rs 3,600 for the stores supplied late.

q: Advance payment at 98 per cent of the value of stores is made to a supplier against the inspection certificate and despatch documents on a bill of Rs 8,40,000. The balance amount payable to the supplier after the material has been received, inspected and accepted at the destination depot is:
e: Advance at 98 per cent leaves a balance of 2 per cent of Rs 8,40,000 = Rs 16,800, payable after the material is received, inspected and accepted at destination.

q: A depot holds 2,400 units of an item. Its book rate is revised from Rs 45 per unit to Rs 38 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand consequent on this revision, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 2,400 x (Rs 45 - Rs 38) = 2,400 x Rs 7 = Rs 16,800, debited through the Stock Adjustment Account on downward revision of book rate.

q: A depot holds 400 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 25 per unit. A fresh receipt of 200 units of the item is taken into stock at Rs 40 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item is:
e: Stock value = 400 x Rs 25 + 200 x Rs 40 = Rs 10,000 + Rs 8,000 = Rs 18,000 for 600 units, giving a revised average book rate of Rs 30 per unit.

q: During stock verification of a depot, a shortage of 18 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 850 per unit. The value of the shortage to be brought to account is:
e: Shortage value at book rate = 18 units x Rs 850 = Rs 15,300, to be brought to account through stock verification adjustment.

q: During stock verification of a depot, 30 units of an item are found physically in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 125 per unit. On the excess being taken on stock after approval, the amount credited through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Excess taken on stock is credited through the Stock Adjustment Account at book rate: 30 units x Rs 125 = Rs 3,750.

q: A stores depot issues 380 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 110 per unit, to a railway workshop for use on a manufacturing job in hand. The value of this issue is initially debited to:
e: Stores issued to a workshop for a manufacturing job are initially debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, from which the cost is later transferred to the finished job or asset.

q: A depot issues 240 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 180 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 12 per cent of the book value, as given in the conditions of issue. The total amount recoverable from the outside party is:
e: Book value is 240 x Rs 180 = Rs 43,200. Adding departmental charges at 12 per cent, Rs 5,184, the amount recoverable from the outside party is Rs 48,384.

q: An imported stores item is invoiced at Rs 4,20,000. The freight paid on it is Rs 36,000, the insurance premium Rs 9,000 and the customs duty Rs 45,000. The value at which the item is taken into stock in the priced accounts, being its landed cost, is:
e: Landed cost = invoice + freight + insurance + customs duty = Rs 4,20,000 + Rs 36,000 + Rs 9,000 + Rs 45,000 = Rs 5,10,000, at which the item is taken into stock.

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot delays lifting the material for 12 days beyond the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 375 per day for the period of delay, as per the conditions of sale given to him. The ground rent payable by him is:
e: Ground rent for delayed lifting = 12 days x Rs 375 per day = Rs 4,500, payable by the purchaser under the conditions of sale.

q: Four wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 5 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading them. Demurrage is leviable at Rs 1,500 per wagon per day, as given. The total demurrage payable in respect of these wagons is:
e: Demurrage = 4 wagons x 5 days x Rs 1,500 per wagon per day = Rs 30,000 for detention beyond the free time allowed for unloading.

q: A field official holds a stores imprest of a fixed quantity of 900 units of an item. At the time of replenishment he holds 340 units on hand and renders an account of consumption of 560 units. The quantity to be supplied to him in replenishment of the imprest is:
e: In a fixed imprest, replenishment equals consumption accounted for: 900 - 340 on hand = 560 units, restoring the imprest to its fixed quantity.

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of an item is 14,400 units. The stock in hand is 1,800 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 600 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Coverage = (stock in hand + dues) in months of AAC: (1,800 + 600) / 14,400 x 12 = 2 months of consumption cover.

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item is 7,200 units and coverage for four months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 700 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 500 units. The quantity required to be ordered is:
e: Quantity required for 4 months = 7,200 x 4/12 = 2,400 units. Less stock 700 and dues 500, quantity to order = 2,400 - 1,200 = 1,200 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,250 units and the re-order quantity is 950 units. The minimum consumption is 60 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,250 + 950 - (60 x 5) = 1,900 units.

q: The re-order level of a stock item is 1,050 units. Its average consumption is 75 units per week and the average lead time is 6 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 1,050 - (75 x 6) = 1,050 - 450 = 600 units.

q: The average consumption of a stock item is 48 units per day and the lead time for its emergency procurement, as given, is 5 days. The danger level of the item is:
e: Danger level = average consumption x emergency procurement lead time = 48 units per day x 5 days = 240 units.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 210 units per week, its normal consumption is 170 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 5 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item, worked out on the excess of maximum over normal consumption during the lead time, is:
e: Safety stock for lead-time variation in consumption = (maximum - normal consumption) x lead time = (210 - 170) x 5 = 40 x 5 = 200 units.

q: The minimum stock level of an item is 520 units and its maximum stock level is 1,880 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (520 + 1,880) / 2 = 1,200 units.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 90 lakh. The inventory carrying cost is estimated at 18 per cent per annum of the average stock value, as given. The annual inventory carrying cost of the railway is:
e: Annual carrying cost = 18 per cent of Rs 90 lakh average stock value = Rs 16,20,000 per annum.

q: During a year, the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is debited with Rs 1,45,000 on account of shortages found in stock verification and Rs 35,000 on account of price differences, and is credited with Rs 60,000 on account of excesses found in stock verification. The net balance of the account, which is cleared at the close of the year under the sanction of the competent authority, is:
e: Debits are Rs 1,45,000 + Rs 35,000 = Rs 1,80,000; credits are Rs 60,000. The net balance is a debit of Rs 1,20,000, cleared at year end under competent sanction.

q: The Purchase Suspense account of a railway opens with a debit balance of Rs 5 lakh. During the month, bills amounting to Rs 18 lakh are paid and material amounting to Rs 20 lakh is received and linked against bills already paid. The closing balance of the account is:

options.A: A credit balance of Rs 2 lakh
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 23 lakh
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 3 lakh

e: Purchase Suspense: opening debit Rs 5 lakh + bills paid Rs 18 lakh - material received and linked Rs 20 lakh = a closing debit balance of Rs 3 lakh.

q: Two balances relating to the stores of a railway are under review: the first represents the value of stores physically held in depots and borne in the priced stock accounts, and the second represents amounts lying under the stores suspense heads awaiting linking or final adjustment. For the purposes of the half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts:

options.A: Both the stock balances and the suspense balances are covered, and the priced ledger balances are proved with the balances in the general books
options.B: Only the stock balances are covered, suspense balances being excluded altogether
options.C: Only the suspense balances are covered, stock balances being excluded altogether
options.D: Neither balance is covered, the statement relating only to tenders opened in the half year

e: The half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts covers both priced stock balances and stores suspense balances, and priced ledger balances are proved with the general books balances.

q: During a period, a depot receives 150 demands for a stock item and is able to meet 135 of them in full from the stock held. The level of service rendered by the depot in respect of the item, expressed as the percentage of demands met in full, is:
e: Service level = demands met in full / total demands x 100 = 135 / 150 x 100 = 90 per cent.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 9,600 units and the quantity ordered each time, as given, is 600 units. The number of orders placed for the item during the year is:
e: Number of orders = annual requirement / quantity per order = 9,600 / 600 = 16 orders during the year.

q: The Turnover Ratio of the stores of a railway is 0.32 and the closing balance of its stores is Rs 96 lakh. The total issues of stores of the railway during the year are:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues, so total issues = Rs 96 lakh / 0.32 = Rs 300 lakh, i.e. Rs 3 crore.

q:
Consider the following statements about auctions and procurement on Indian Railways:
1. Scrap and unserviceable stores are disposed of by e-auction conducted on the IREPS portal.
2. In the purchase of stores, a reverse auction conducted on IREPS is a method of obtaining competitive rates from suppliers.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Scrap and unserviceable stores are disposed of by e-auction on IREPS, and reverse auction on IREPS is also a method of obtaining competitive rates in purchase of stores; both are correct.

q: At the end of a month, a railway has paid suppliers' bills amounting to Rs 46 lakh for stores, but the material against those bills has not yet been received at any depot. Pending receipt of the material, the amount so paid stands as a debit balance under:
e: Bills paid for stores not yet received at any depot stand as a debit balance under Purchase Suspense, pending receipt and linking of the material.

q:
Consider the following statements about Sales Suspense:
1. Sales Suspense is credited when the purchaser of scrap deposits the sale value with the Railway.
2. A debit balance under Sales Suspense indicates that the sale value has been deposited by the purchaser but the material has not yet been delivered to him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: Sales Suspense is credited when the purchaser deposits the sale value. Statement 2 is wrong: a debit balance under Sales Suspense arises when material has been delivered but the sale value not yet received, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: At the close of a year, the closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 66 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 5.5 crore. The Turnover Ratio of the stores of the railway is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 66 lakh / Rs 550 lakh = 0.12.

q: Which of the following differences is NOT adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account?

options.A: Price (value) differences arising on revision of the book rate of an item
options.B: Quantity differences between the physical balance and the book balance found in stock verification
options.C: The difference between the sale value and the book value of scrap sold
options.D: Bills paid to suppliers for material which has not yet been received

e: Bills paid for material not yet received are held under Purchase Suspense, not Stock Adjustment Account, which covers only price differences, verification differences and sale-versus-book differences.

q: Stores in a depot have been declared dead surplus and have been circulated to other depots and railways, but no depot or railway has come forward to take them. The dead surplus stores are then finally disposed of by:

options.A: Returning them to the original suppliers free of cost
options.C: Keeping them in the depot indefinitely without any entry
options.D: Issuing them free to the stores staff

e: Dead surplus stores circulated to other depots and railways but not taken by any of them are finally disposed of by sale as scrap.

q: Item M has an annual consumption of 250 units at a book rate of Rs 800 per unit. Item N has an annual consumption of 9,000 units at a book rate of Rs 15 per unit. For the purpose of ABC classification, the correct position is that:

options.A: Item M ranks higher than Item N, its annual consumption value being Rs 2,00,000 against Rs 1,35,000 of Item N
options.B: Item N ranks higher than Item M, because a larger number of units of Item N is consumed
options.C: Both items rank equal, because ABC classification is based on quantity alone
options.D: Neither item can be classified, because ABC classification is based on weight

e: ABC ranking is by annual consumption value: Item M = 250 x Rs 800 = Rs 2,00,000, Item N = 9,000 x Rs 15 = Rs 1,35,000, so Item M ranks higher despite fewer units.

q: A depot issues stores to a divisional office for routine maintenance work charged to revenue (working expenses). In the allocation of expenditure, issues of stores to revenue heads are linked to:
e: Stores issued for revenue working expenses are allocated under Primary Unit 27, the stores/material primary unit used for issues to revenue heads in the railway classification of expenditure.

q: A quantity of stores is held in the custody of a user department at a station, outside the stores depot. The physical verification of such stores is carried out by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper of the issuing depot
options.B: The Stock Verifiers of the Accounts Department in all cases
options.C: The Travelling Inspector of Stores Accounts
options.D: Officers of the department holding the stores

e: Stores held outside a depot in the custody of a user department are physically verified by officers of the department holding the stores, not by the depot storekeeper or stock verifiers.

q: During stock verification of a depot, the stock verifier finds no difference in quantities, but notices that bin cards are not being posted regularly and receipts are not being entered promptly. Such procedural irregularities are brought out by the stock verifier through:
e: Procedural irregularities noticed during stock verification, such as unposted bin cards and delayed receipt entries, are brought out by the stock verifier in a narrative report.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. AAC, in stores inventory control, stands for Average Annual Consumption.
2. After the model SOP of 2018, vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is required only for A-category items.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: AAC stands for Average Annual Consumption, and under the model SOP of 2018, Headquarters Finance vetting of AAC is required only for A-category items; both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following does NOT bring stores into a depot as a recognised source of supply under Para 201 of the Stores Code, Vol. I?

options.A: Purchases made through tenders and contracts
options.B: Manufacture of stores in railway workshops
options.C: Returns of stores to the depot by consuming departments
options.D: Sale of scrap lying in the depot to purchasers

e: Para 201 of the Stores Code, Vol. I lists purchases, workshop manufacture and returns from departments as sources bringing stores into a depot; sale of scrap is a disposal, not a source of supply.

q: A rate contract for an item has been concluded with a firm at a fixed rate. During the currency of the contract, a depot requires a quantity of the item. The depot obtains the supply by:

options.A: Placing a supply order on the firm under the rate contract, as and when required
options.B: Inviting a fresh open tender for that quantity
options.C: Purchasing the item from the open market at the prevailing rate
options.D: Waiting until the rate contract expires and a new contract is concluded

e: Under a rate contract at a fixed rate, the depot obtains supplies as required by placing a supply order on the firm under the contract, without inviting a fresh tender each time.

q: A Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) furnished in support of a stores demand certifies that:

options.A: The firm named in the certificate is the cheapest supplier in the market
options.B: The article is a proprietary article manufactured by a particular firm and no other firm manufactures or supplies the same article
options.C: The article is exempted from inspection before acceptance
options.D: The article will be supplied free of security deposit in all cases

e: A Proprietary Article Certificate certifies that the article is a proprietary article manufactured by a particular firm and no other firm manufactures or supplies the same article.

q: A purchase officer proposes to dispose of a lot of scrap lying in a depot by holding a reverse auction on IREPS. This proposal is not in order because, on Indian Railways:

options.A: Reverse auction cannot be held on IREPS at all
options.B: Scrap can be sold only by open tender
options.C: Reverse auction on IREPS is used for purchase of stores, whereas scrap is disposed of by e-auction
options.D: Reverse auction is reserved for sale of surplus land

e: Reverse auction on IREPS is a purchasing method for obtaining competitive rates; scrap and unserviceable stores are disposed of by e-auction, so a reverse auction for scrap disposal is not in order.

q: A supplier defaults on an order for 400 units of an item at Rs 210 per unit. After cancelling the order for the defaulted quantity and giving due notice, the Railway makes a risk purchase of the same quantity at Rs 245 per unit. The excess cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Risk purchase excess = (Rs 245 - Rs 210) x 400 = Rs 35 x 400 = Rs 14,000, recoverable from the defaulting supplier after cancellation and due notice.

q: A firm registered with NSIC claims that, because it is exempted from furnishing Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders, it is also exempted from furnishing Security Deposit after acceptance of its tender. The claim is:

options.A: Correct, the exemption covers both deposits
options.B: Not correct, the exemption recognised in stores tenders is from Earnest Money Deposit, and Security Deposit remains payable on acceptance of the tender
options.C: Correct, provided the firm is also RDSO-approved
options.D: Not correct, because such firms are exempted only from liquidated damages

e: The recognised exemption for NSIC-registered and similar firms is from Earnest Money Deposit only; Security Deposit remains payable after acceptance of the tender, so the claim is not correct.

q: While framing its annual procurement plan, a railway is required to ensure that the minimum percentage of its annual procurement of goods and services made from Micro and Small Enterprises is:
e: Government procurement policy requires at least 25 per cent of annual procurement of goods and services to be made from Micro and Small Enterprises.

q: A supplier offers an item in a stores tender and declares that the local content of the item offered by him is 60 per cent. Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, the supplier is classified as a:
e: Under the Make in India Order, a supplier with local content of 50 per cent or more is a Class-I local supplier; 60 per cent declared local content falls in Class-I.

q:
Consider the following statements about the e-auction of scrap:
1. The highest bid received in an e-auction results in a concluded sale only after the bid is accepted by the competent authority.
2. Earnest money deposited by bidders who remain unsuccessful in the e-auction is refunded to them after finalisation of the auction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The highest e-auction bid concludes a sale only on acceptance by the competent authority, and earnest money of unsuccessful bidders is refunded after finalisation; both statements are correct.

q: In the Stores Budget of a railway, if the deduct entry in respect of stores issues were omitted altogether, the consequence would be that:

options.A: No funds would be available for purchase of stores
options.B: The closing balance of stores would become nil
options.C: Suppliers' bills could not be paid during the year
options.D: The value of the same stores would be budgeted twice, once in the Stores Budget and again in the estimates of the consuming departments

e: Stores issues carry a deduct entry in the Stores Budget because the same stores are charged in consuming departments' estimates; omitting it would budget the value of the same stores twice.

q: The statement of the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is annexed to the:

options.A: Finance Accounts of the Central Government

e: The statement of the Stock Adjustment Account is annexed to the Appropriation Accounts of the railway, showing shortages, excesses and price differences adjusted during the year.

q: A stores contract is placed at the rate of Rs 340 per unit and contains a fall clause. During the currency of the contract, the supplier sells the same item to another buyer at Rs 315 per unit. The rate payable by the Railway for supplies under its contract is:

options.A: Rs 340 per unit, the contract rate being unalterable
options.B: Rs 327.50 per unit, being the average of the two rates
options.C: Rs 355 per unit, after adding departmental charges
options.D: Rs 315 per unit, the lower rate at which the supplier has sold the item to another buyer

e: Under the fall clause, the lower rate of Rs 315 at which the supplier sold the item to another buyer becomes the rate payable by the Railway under its contract.

q: An Accounts official has to ascertain, for a stores item, both the quantity transacted and the value at which the transaction has been accounted for. The record which gives him both the quantities and the values of stores transactions is the:

options.A: Bin Card maintained at the bin

e: The Priced Stores Ledger records both quantities transacted and the values at which transactions are accounted, unlike the bin card which records quantities only.

q: A clerk maintains that the Price Ledger (PL) Number allotted to a stores item consists of six digits. The correct position is that a PL Number consists of:
e: A Price Ledger (PL) Number allotted to a stores item under the Stores Code codification consists of 8 digits, covering group, class and the specific item.

q: Form DS-8 in a railway stores depot is the form used for the:

options.A: Receipt Note, prepared when material is received, inspected and accepted into stock
options.B: Issue Note, prepared when material is issued to a consuming department
options.C: Stock Sheet, prepared when a difference is found in stock verification
options.D: Bin Card, maintained at the bin of the item

e: Form DS-8 is the Receipt Note, prepared in a stores depot when material is received, inspected and accepted into stock.

q: A supplier's bill is put up for payment supported only by the purchase order, the receipt note for the material not having been received in the Accounts office. The bill cannot be passed at this stage because, before payment, the Accounts office is required to link together:

options.A: The tender notice and the comparative statement only
options.B: The bin card and the stock sheet only
options.C: The inspection note and the auction catalogue only
options.D: The purchase order, the receipt note and the bill together

e: Before a supplier's bill is passed, Accounts must link the purchase order, the receipt note and the bill together to establish that the material billed for was ordered and received.

q: Under the system of uniform pricing of stores followed on a railway, it is ensured that:

options.A: Every item in stock is issued at one and the same price
options.B: The issue (book) rate of an item is the same in all the depots of the railway
options.C: Every supplier quotes the same rate for an item
options.D: Issue rates of all items are revised on the first of every month

e: Under uniform pricing, the issue or book rate of an item is the same in all depots of the railway, so consuming departments are charged uniformly wherever they draw the item.

q: For a high-value stores purchase, a Tender Committee is constituted with members from the Stores and the Executive departments, but with no member from the Finance/Accounts Department. The constitution of the committee is defective because a Stores Tender Committee dealing with high-value purchases must include a member from the:
e: A Stores Tender Committee for high-value purchases must include a Finance/Accounts member along with Stores and Executive members; a committee without Finance representation is defectively constituted.

q: Stores purchase contracts placed by Indian Railways on suppliers are governed by the standard conditions known as the:

options.A: IRS (Indian Railway Standard) Conditions of Contract
options.B: General Conditions of Contract for works only
options.C: Conditions printed on the GeM portal only
options.D: Indian Contract Act, with no standard conditions of any kind

e: Stores purchase contracts on Indian Railways are governed by the IRS (Indian Railway Standard) Conditions of Contract, the standard conditions for supply contracts.

q: A purchase office invites tenders for a stores item by issuing the tender notice to the public at large through a press advertisement, open to any firm that responds. Such a tender is NOT a limited tender, because a limited tender is invited from:

options.A: A single firm chosen by the depot officer
options.B: Firms selected by draw of lots
options.C: Any firm responding to a press advertisement
options.D: A limited number of approved/registered firms

e: A limited tender is invited from a limited number of approved or registered firms; a tender open to the public at large through press advertisement is an open tender, not a limited tender.
